QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_73

question.text: An anchor investor asks Mr. Devendra to negotiate an operating-expense cap as a percentage of commitments. Which framing is MOST consistent with the workbook's treatment of operating-expense caps and investor disclosure?

answer.text: Refuse any cap; investors must accept whatever expenses the manager incurs
Negotiate an operating-expense cap within the typical 10-50 bps range, disclose the expense categories covered and their limits, and document the cap in the fund documents
Agree to any cap only if the investor waives MFN rights
Agree to a cap and absorb all overruns from the management fee with no further disclosure

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook supports operating-expense caps in the 10-50 bps range, contemplates investor negotiation of such caps, and requires disclosure of the expense types and limits in the fund documents. Negotiating within that range and disclosing the covered categories is consistent with the source. The Trap: Option A ignores the negotiation and disclosure framework. Option C ties an unrelated MFN concession to a routine cap negotiation. Option D pushes all overruns into the management fee without proper disclosure or framework. Note: Expense caps should be sized within market range and accompanied by clear disclosure of what is and is not covered.
